title: FIRST CONTACT: STOP BEFORE THE GLASS
subtitle: A three-minute experiment about sensing, estimation, and safe stopping.
briefing: Drive wheels create traction; passive casters carry load and swivel freely.
The LiDAR reports timed ranges from its mounted sensor frame. It does not report world truth.
The emergency safety layer uses fresh observations and the robot's own braking model.
Reach the marked stop pose before the glass door and remain stable.

walkaround.title: DRIVE WHEELS / TRACTION
walkaround.lesson: Each drive wheel has one rolling joint. Differential steering comes from left-right wheel speed, so these wheels never swivel like steering wheels.

walkaround.title: PASSIVE CASTER / SUPPORT
walkaround.lesson: The caster carries load through two passive joints: a vertical swivel and a horizontal wheel roll. Neither joint is a drive command.

walkaround.title: LIDAR / TIMED RANGES
walkaround.lesson: The blue scanner reports ranges from this configured sensor frame. It measures surfaces; it does not reveal actor identities, scripts, or world truth.

walkaround.title: COMPUTE, SAFETY, AND CHASSIS
walkaround.lesson: The onboard robot turns timestamped measurements into estimates and commands. A separate fresh-observation safety layer may stop motion before higher-level planning reacts.

prediction.question: What evidence may independently command the final safety stop?

choices.label: The actor's hidden scripted route and exact world pose
choices.explanation: Those are SIM-only truth. They may appear in replay or scoring, but never enter the deployable robot.

choices.label: Fresh LiDAR ranges, measured speed, and the robot's braking model
choices.explanation: Correct. The final safety monitor can stop from local observations even when global localization is uncertain.

choices.label: The global map and goal estimate alone
choices.explanation: A global map cannot represent every new obstacle or sensor timeout. It is insufficient as the final safety authority.

running_prompt: Observe the physical robot first. Press L for ROBOT LiDAR, E for truth-vs-estimate, and T for deterministic Turbo.

lessons: Sensors provide measurements; perception and localization build estimates from them.
ROBOT completion and SIM truth arrival are checked separately.
Collision is a hard failure. Speed, smoothness, or energy cannot compensate for it.
